open.description:
Open an actor in the list's own detail, as a row click (`drilled: false`, beside the list) or
a double click (`drilled: true`, instead of it) would — past the open actor's unsaved-changes
guard, and into the block route like any opening. For a page that learns of an actor
elsewhere (a create flow, a search) and wants it shown here. Nothing opens while both row
actions are `event`.

actorClick.description: Fired when an actor row is single-clicked — the page's own click handling under `rowClickAction: 'event'`.

actorCreated.description:
An actor was created from the list's «Create actor» (on a Scripts list: «Create smart form»,
whose `actorId` is the new form's `appId` and which also carries its `ref`; on a Graphs list:
«Create graph», the new graph — bind it to the graph editor to land on its first layer).

actorDoubleClick.description: Fired when an actor row is double-clicked — the page's own handling under `rowDoubleClickAction: 'event'`.

exportQueueOpened.description:
«Open» was pressed on «Added to the export queue» (with `exportQueueLink`): show the queue. Last, so
a binding added in an editor still starts on the block's primary event.

rowAction.description:
One of `rowActions` was chosen on a row — ActorView's `onAction` shape, plus the row's `ref`
and `formId` (a page building a link to the actor needs them, and has no read of its own).

accId.description: Workspace id whose actors are listed. Falls back to the active workspace.

anyOf.description:
Offer the toolbar's «Create actor» (opens the CreateActor block on the list's Account
Template, or with none when the list is not narrowed to one; a list pinned to the Scripts
system form by `formTitle` offers «Create smart form», the CreateSmartForm wizard, instead,
and one pinned to Graphs offers «Create graph», which makes a graph with its first layer at
once — no dialog — and emits `actorCreated` for it).
Off for a read-only page.

Default: `true`.

Pin the list to actors whose `data.<key>` holds one of the listed values, e.g. only v2 smart
forms: `{ "cduVersion": [2, "2"] }`. A number never matches its string spelling, so list both
when writers disagree. Not a user-visible filter (no chip); search keeps to the pinned set, and
saved filters with stored conditions are not offered as tabs.

Rows per page; `ActorListApp` defaults it to 20. `.optional()`, not `.default()` — no Zod
parse runs on the render path, and `gen-cdu-schema.mjs` refuses a zod default.

defaultTabId.description: Tab id the list opens on. Matches one of the preset tab ids.

anyOf.description:
Seeds the initial "Columns" visibility. Omitted keys stay visible; the
toolbar's Columns picker still lets a user toggle anything.

Offer «Open» on «Added to the export queue»; pressing it emits `exportQueueOpened`, which the
page binds to wherever it shows Import & Export. Off by default: without a binding it would
lead nowhere.
Pin the list to one Account Template. Omit = all forms.

formTitle.description: Pin to a system form by title (e.g. "Graphs"), resolved via `form/system/list`. Ignored when `formId` is set.

anyOf.description:
Per-label text overrides; every entry is optional and falls back to the kit
dictionary for the active language, so a page localizes one string by binding
it — `{ "labels": { "actorList.search.placeholder": "{{ $locale.searchActors }}" } }`.

The page's own items in each row's actions menu, before the built-in ones — ActorView's
`header.actions` shape, serializable: choosing one emits `rowAction` and the page binds what
it does (open the smart form in production, start a process, …). `icon` is a kit icon name.
Not offered on the Trash tab: a deleted actor has nothing to act on.

What a single click on a row does. `panel` (the default) opens the actor beside the list, as
legacy's actor list does; `drill` replaces the list with the actor's page until Back; `event`
opens nothing, so the page handles the click itself by binding `actorClick`. `actorClick` is
emitted in every mode; a Trash row never opens anything.

The same for a double click; `drill` by default — legacy opened the actor's own page. Set
`event` when the page binds `actorDoubleClick` itself (e.g. to open a smart-form editor).

Shows row-selection checkboxes and the bulk-action bar.

Default: `true`.

openedActorId.description: The actor currently open in the panel or detail; absent after closing or returning to the list.

openedActorMode.description: The current row's presentation; lets a host retain list chrome beside a panel and hide it only for drill-in.

onBlur.description: Fires when the button loses focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onClick.description: Fires when the button is clicked, but not while it is disabled or `loading`; `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onFocus.description: Fires when the button receives focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onMouseEnter.description: Fires when the pointer moves onto the button; `$event` is the DOM mouse event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onMouseLeave.description: Fires when the pointer moves off the button; `$event` is the DOM mouse event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

ButtonType.description: Tonal keeps a tinted surface at rest without the emphasis of a filled action. `field` wears a filled field's own surface (`surfaceField`), for a control that stands in for a field in a row of them — a search folded to its icon, say. It is neutral by design: `variant` does not tint it.

props.description:
Serializable CDU props for the Button primitive — the single source of truth.

Passthrough keys are `Pick`ed from the component (enums/scalars flow from `@simulator-ui-kit/types`, so they are never re-spelled here). The remaining fields are adapter-only stand-ins for the non-serializable component props: `title` (→ `children`) and icon **names** (→ `ComponentIconConfig` via the icon registry).

ariaLabel.description: Accessible name — REQUIRED for icon-only buttons (no `title` text).

anyOf.description: Expand icon direction to display after endIcon Shows ArrowUp2Icon when 'up' or ArrowDown2Icon when 'down'
Whether the button should take full width
Whether the button is in a loading state
Size of the button
Visual type of the button
Variant of the button
Visibility state

onClick.description: Fires when the card is clicked — or, when `interactive`, activated with Enter/Space; `$event` is the DOM event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

CardShadow.description: Card elevation — the shared  {@link  Shadow }  scale plus two Card-only levels: `overlay`, for panels floating above a canvas (edge ring + tight contact + small ambient), and `floating`, for a card over the page itself — a call or a meeting reminder — that must lift off a white page (see both tokens in themes). They stay local to Card so the shared layout-band `shadow` (docked chrome) keeps its deliberate xs/sm ceiling.

CardSquareCorner.description: A single square corner for directional surfaces such as message bubbles.

SurfaceRole.description: Content stays opaque; navigation may use the theme's translucent control material.

props.description: CDU props for `Card` — a surface container. Content comes from the tree node's `children`; `title` is a plain string prop on the component (no adapter). Colours are restricted to `SurfaceColorToken` by the component type itself, per the "closed component, open theme" rule.

anyOf.description: Leading accent bar in a semantic status colour. Wins the border over  {@link  identityHue }  when both are set — see that prop's own doc comment.
Arrow placement relative to the card If provided, displays an arrow pointing in the specified direction
Background color of the card — semantic tokens only (e.g., 'surfaceSubtle', 'surfaceSuccess', 'surfaceInverse', 'background') Overrides variant-specific background colors
Text color for the card content — semantic tokens only (e.g., 'text', 'textStrong', 'textSecondary', 'foreground') Children elements will inherit this color Overrides variant-specific text colors
Custom padding sizes for each side using CSS shorthand syntax When customSize is provided, size prop is ignored for padding
Font size for the card content Children elements will inherit this size
Whether the card should take full height
Whether the card should take full width

Make the card behave as a clickable control: pointer cursor, hover/active surfaces, and full keyboard support. When set, the card renders with `role="button"`, is focusable, and activates on Enter/Space. Provide `onClick` to handle activation.
Selected/active visual state (primary tint + border). When the card is `interactive`, this is also reflected as `aria-pressed`.
Box shadow of the card
Size of the card (padding)
Removes the radius from one corner while preserving the card's other radii. Useful for directional surfaces such as incoming and outgoing message bubbles.
Navigation chrome adopts a theme's control material; content keeps its ordinary surface.

title.description: Optional title displayed at the top of the card with underline

anyOf.description: Visual variant of the card. `control` provides a contrasting boundary and field surface for composite inputs.
Visibility state

props.description: CDU props for `Col` (the Grid column) — span/offset/push/pull, order, flex and the responsive breakpoint configs (`xs`–`xxl`, each a bare span or a full responsive config). The gutter is not a Col prop: it comes from the enclosing `Row` through context. `minWidth` / `minHeight` are the same flex knobs `Row` exposes: a column in a non-wrapping row only shrinks below its content's width with `minWidth` (a chat list column that folds into its avatar rail).

anyOf.description: Flex property for the column
Responsive configuration for lg screens (≥1200px)
Responsive configuration for md screens (≥992px)
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic height by setting `min-height: 0`. Required for a nested scroll area inside a flex column.
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic width by setting `min-width: 0`. Required to let a flex child truncate its own children (e.g. an ellipsised Label inside a row).
Number of columns to offset from the left
Order of the column
Number of columns to pull to the left
Number of columns to push to the right
Responsive configuration for sm screens (≥768px)
Number of columns to span (1-24)
Responsive configuration for xl screens (≥1600px)
Responsive configuration for xs screens (≥576px)
Responsive configuration for xxl screens (≥1920px)

onCancel.description: Fires when the Cancel button is clicked or Escape is pressed in the calendar, after the pending selection is discarded; `$event` is empty.

onChange.description: Fires only when the user confirms with OK, never while picking and never with `null`; `$event` is `{ startDate, endDate, timeZoneOffset, recurrence? }` — Unix seconds (`endDate` equals `startDate` for a single date), the offset in minutes, and `recurrence` present only when the `recurrence` prop is on (`null` while Repeat is off).

onOk.description: Fires when the OK button is clicked, after `onChange` (and even when nothing was picked); `$event` is empty.

DatePickerLabels.description:
Labels for all user-visible text in the DatePicker.

Each entry defaults to the `datePicker.<key>` message of the active `LocaleProvider` language, so a translated app needs no `labels` at all; pass one to override a single string (this is what a CDU page binds `$locale` to).

dateRange.description: Label beside the single ⇄ range toggle (`rangeToggle`).

endHours.description: Label for the end hours column (range mode).

endMinutes.description: Label for the end minutes column (range mode).

endTime.description: Label for the end time picker field (range mode).

frequency.description: Accessible name for the frequency select. Not rendered — the options carry the units, so the field itself has no visible text to name it.

frequencyDay.description: Daily option in the frequency select.

frequencyMonth.description: Monthly option in the frequency select.

frequencyWeek.description: Weekly option in the frequency select.

hours.description: Label for the hours column (single mode).

minutes.description: Label for the minutes column (single mode).

now.description: Label for the Now button (sets current time).

ok.description: Label for the OK / confirm button.

repeat.description: Label beside the recurrence on/off toggle.

startHours.description: Label for the start hours column (range mode).

startMinutes.description: Label for the start minutes column (range mode).

startTime.description: Label for the start time picker field (range mode).

time.description: Label for the time picker field (single mode).

weekDays.description: Accessible name for the weekday button group.

DatePickerRecurrence.description:
A recurrence rule.

Field-for-field identical to what the legacy `mw-style-react` `Calendar` emits (`freq`/`interval`/`byDay`/`count`), so an app can move between the two libraries with no mapper. Note this is NOT RFC 5545 iCalendar: `byDay` is a numeric JS weekday, not `MO`/`TU`. A consumer integrating with a calendar API converts it itself.

anyOf.description: Weekdays for a weekly rule, as JS day numbers: 0=Sun, 1=Mon … 6=Sat. Omitted entirely when `freq` is not `'weekly'`. Never empty on a committed weekly rule — the picker falls back to the start date's own weekday so the rule is unambiguous for whoever expands the series.
Number of occurrences before the rule ends — `RECURRENCE_MIN`…`RECURRENCE_MAX_COUNT`.
Repeat unit.
Repeat every N units — `RECURRENCE_MIN`…`RECURRENCE_MAX_INTERVAL`.

DatePickerRecurrenceFreq.description: How often a recurring selection repeats.

DatePickerValue.description:
Unified value format for both single and range modes

Format: Unix timestamps (seconds, not milliseconds) + timezone offset (minutes) Why seconds? Backend-friendly (PostgreSQL, Go), smaller numbers, easier debugging

Timezone convention: follows JS Date.getTimezoneOffset() (opposite of ISO 8601)
- UTC+5 (e.g., Pakistan) → -300 minutes
- UTC-5 (e.g., New York EST) → +300 minutes

Single mode: startDate === endDate Range mode: startDate <= endDate (auto-sorted on selection). A single click picks a one-day range, so without `showTime` (or with equal start/end times) startDate === endDate there too

anyOf.description: Unix timestamp in seconds (= startDate in single mode)

Recurrence rule for the selection, or `null` when the Repeat toggle is off.

Present only when the `recurrence` prop is enabled — the key is absent entirely otherwise, so a one-off selection emits exactly the payload it always has.
Unix timestamp in seconds
Timezone offset in minutes, JS convention (same as Date.getTimezoneOffset())

props.description: CDU props for `DatePicker` (an always-open calendar panel). All keys are pure passthrough of the component's serializable props. `value`/`defaultValue` are the unified timestamp shape (`DatePickerValue | null`); `labels` is the all-string localization map. The `disabledDate` predicate callback is not modelled (non-serializable).

anyOf.description: Initial uncontrolled value.
Custom labels for buttons and select fields. Use to localize the component or override default English text. Unspecified keys fall back to their English defaults.

locale.description: Locale for month and weekday names (BCP 47 language tag). Accepts both full tags (`"en-US"`, `"uk-UA"`) and short tags (`"en"`, `"fr"`). Short tags are automatically expanded via `Intl.Locale.maximize()` for week start detection. Defaults to the active `LocaleProvider` language, or `'en'` without a provider.

anyOf.description:
Selection mode.
- `'single'` — picks one date (startDate === endDate in the emitted value)
- `'range'` — picks a start and end date

Whether to show the Repeat section below the calendar — an on/off toggle that reveals frequency, interval, weekday and occurrence-count controls.

Opt-in: with this off (the default) the panel renders exactly as before and the emitted value carries no `recurrence` key at all. With it on, the rule is committed alongside the date by the OK button as  {@link  DatePickerValue.recurrence } , and is `null` while the toggle is off.
Whether to show time picker (hours and minutes)
Whether to show timezone selector (only available when showTime is true)

Size of the date picker. Controls the density of the always-open calendar panel (cell and header sizes), not a row-control height — the DatePicker is a panel and does not sit on the shared control scale.
Use 12-hour time format with an AM/PM column (only available when showTime is true)
Controlled value.
Visibility state

First day of the week: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday. If omitted, auto-detected from `locale` via `Intl.Locale.getWeekInfo()` / `weekInfo`. Falls back to 1 (Monday, ISO standard) if the browser does not support week info.

FormFieldRuleCdu.description: One declared field of a  {@link  FormCduProps } : where it lives and how it validates.

props.description:
CDU props for `Form` — the host-form bridge. This catalog does NOT register it: the renderer ships it (`formPrimitive`, `cdu-renderer/src/forms/Form.primitive.tsx`) and `cdu-harness` `buildRegistry` adds it next to the catalog, so every host renders it.

Its contract lives here because this is what the save-time validators read — sim-api (`internal/cdu/catalog`, synced by `make sync-cdu-schema`) and the smart-form editor. Without it a stored page could not hold a `Form`, and `form.submit` would send the process an empty `formData` (the values live under `vm[valueKey]`, read through the Form).

Mirrors the Zod `props` of `Form.primitive.tsx`; `cdu-harness` asserts the two agree.

anyOf.description: Field rules driving `form.validate` (`vm.errors[valueKey]` / `vm.valid[valueKey]`).

valueKey.description: The vm key holding this form's values (default: the form id). Values live at `vm[valueKey]`.

props.description: Serializable CDU props for the `Label` primitive. Passthrough keys flow their enum/scalar types straight from `LabelProps`; `text` is an adapter stand-in routed to the component's `children`.

anyOf.description: Text alignment
Color from the design system palette
Whether the label is in an error state
Whether the label should grow to fill available space (flex: 1) Useful when the label is a child of a flex container and should take remaining space
Clamp the text to N lines with a trailing ellipsis (multi-line truncation). For single-line truncation use `overflow="cut"` instead. Mutually exclusive with `overflow` — `lines` wins if both are set.

maxWidth.description: Maximum width of the label Useful for constraining label width and enabling text wrapping

anyOf.description: How to handle text overflow (single line): `cut` = ellipsis, `break` = wrap.
Whether to show a tooltip with the label content on hover
Font size of the label

text.description: Text child rendered as the label's `children`.

title.description: Custom title attribute for the span element

anyOf.description: Visual variant of the label
Visibility state
Font weight of the label
White space handling Controls how white space and line breaks are handled

props.description: CDU props for `Row` (the Grid row) — horizontal gutter, justification, cross alignment, wrapping, and the flex constraints needed when a row hosts a full-height application region. Columns arrive as tree `children` (`Col` primitives).

anyOf.description: Vertical alignment of flex items
Grow to fill the free space of a flex parent (`flex: 1 1 0%`).
Spacing between columns. A single token sets horizontal spacing; a tuple sets `[horizontal, vertical]` spacing for wrapped rows.
Horizontal alignment of flex items
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic height by setting `min-height: 0`. Required for a nested scroll area inside a flex column.
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic width by setting `min-width: 0`. Required to let a flex child truncate its own children (e.g. an ellipsised Label inside a row).
Whether to wrap items to new lines

onBlur.description: Fires when the field loses focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onChange.description: Fires when the selection changes — an option picked or toggled, a tag removed, or the field cleared; `$event` is `{ value }`, the new value (an array when `multiple`; `undefined`, or `[]` when `multiple`, after a clear).

onClear.description: Fires when the clear button (`clearable`) drops the selection, after `onChange`; `$event` is empty. Clearing only the typed query in an open search does not fire it.

onDeselect.description: Fires in `multiple` mode when an option is removed, by unticking it or removing its tag; `$event` is that option's bare `value`.

onDropdownVisibleChange.description: Fires when the dropdown opens or closes; `$event` is `true` when it opens and `false` when it closes.

onFocus.description: Fires when the field receives focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onKeyDown.description: Fires on each key press in the field; `$event` is the DOM keyboard event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onSearch.description: Fires as the user types in the search field (`searchable`), and with `''` when the query is reset; `$event` is the current search string.

onSelect.description: Fires when the user picks an option (in `multiple` mode, only when adding one), right after `onChange`; `$event` is that option's bare `value`, not `{ value }`.

props.description:
Serializable CDU props for the `Select` primitive — the single source of truth.

Passthrough keys flow straight from `SelectProps` (enums/scalars resolve from the component). Icons and the `options` array are name-based adapter stand-ins: each icon is an icon-registry name (`string`) that the adapter resolves to a `ComponentIconConfig`. The `tagRender`/`filterOption` render-callbacks are not authorable.

anyOf.description: Shows a clear button that resets the current selection

endIcon.description: Trailing trigger icon, by icon-registry name (adapter-resolved).

anyOf.description: Expand icon direction to display instead of endIcon Shows ArrowUp2Icon when 'up' or ArrowDown2Icon when 'down' Takes priority over endIcon when provided

helperTooltip.description: Tooltip text to display next to helper text

anyOf.description: Whether the input is in a loading state Shows spinner instead of icons when true
Maximum height of the dropdown list in pixels
Maximum number of selected-value tags rendered in the trigger before collapsing to a count
Allows selecting more than one option at a time

noDataText.description: Message shown in the dropdown when no options match the current search. Defaults to the kit dictionary — an empty panel must still say something, or it reads as a rendering bug rather than an answer.

anyOf.description: Options with each icon referenced by registry name (adapter-resolved).
Avatar displayed to the left of the label

alt.description: Accessible alt text for the avatar image

anyOf.description: When true, suppresses the auto-generated initials fallback

fallback.description: Fallback text shown when the image fails to load

anyOf.description: Round (people) or rounded-square tile (workspaces, event-type glyphs). Serializable string so it survives the CDU JSON boundary. Defaults to the `Avatar` default (circle).

Identity colour of the initials tile when there is no `src` — the deterministic hue a caller derives from the row's id. Serializable string; falls back to the `Avatar` default. (Distinct from  {@link  SelectOption.color } , which is a standalone dot.)
Badge displayed to the right of the label

content.description: Text or numeric content rendered inside the badge

anyOf.description: Color variant of the badge

color.description: Identity colour (`#rrggbb`) shown as a dot before the label — and, when this option is the selection, before the trigger's text too. A serializable string rather than a node on purpose: options cross the CDU boundary as JSON (see `Select.impl.tsx`, which resolves `icon` from a name), so a ReactNode here would have no way to arrive.

description.description: Secondary line of text shown below the label inside the dropdown

anyOf.description: When true the option is shown but cannot be selected

group.description:
Group key used to visually cluster related options under a heading.

NOT IMPLEMENTED — declared but never read. Headings would break the flat indexing the virtualizer (`virtualItem.index` → `options[index]`) and the keyboard cursor both rely on, so it needs its own pass. `pinned` covers the sectioning our callers actually do.

label.description: Human-readable text displayed in the dropdown and trigger

note.description: A short muted note ON the label's line, after the title — "no access", "archived", "draft". Distinct from `description` (its own second line) and from `tags` (trailing chips): this qualifies the name itself, so it must sit beside it.

anyOf.description: Keep this option ALWAYS visible and at the top of the list: it is exempt from the search filter and floated above the rest. The shape of an «All» / «Any» / «Unassigned» scope row, which must stay reachable however the user has narrowed the list.

Quiet trailing tags — hairline `Chip`s rather than the solid `badge` pill. For the short attributes that disambiguate two similarly-named rows: a kind, a record id, a short hash. `font: 'mono'` keeps a column of ids aligned. A list rather than one, because a row routinely carries a kind AND an id, and they read as one trailing group. Rendered decoratively, so they add no tab stop inside the already-clickable row.

value.description: The underlying value submitted or compared when this option is selected

anyOf.description: Whether the input is read-only
Whether the input is required
Enables searching. Where the user types is decided by  {@link  searchPlacement } .
Size of the select component

startIcon.description: Leading trigger icon, by icon-registry name (adapter-resolved).

anyOf.description: Currently selected value; pass an array when `multiple` is true
Visual variant controlling border and focus-ring color
Enables virtual scrolling for large option lists
Minimum number of options required before virtual scrolling is activated
Visibility state

Booleanish.description: Used to represent DOM API's where users can either pass true or false as a boolean or as its equivalent strings.

LayoutElement.description:
Elements a layout primitive may render.

A closed union rather than full polymorphism: it keeps props inferable, keeps the primitive's own recipe valid (every member is a block-level container), and rules out `as="button"`-style abuse of a layout box as a control.

LayoutLayer.description: Stacking layer for a layered layout child: `back` (behind everything, e.g. a background), `base` (normal content), `dock` (above content, e.g. a dock).

LayoutReveal.description: When a layout child is shown: `hover` hides it until the nearest `hoverScope` ancestor is hovered or focused (always shown on coarse pointers); `always` is the plain default.

PaddingSide.description: A side (or axis) that padding may be applied to. `x` = left + right, `y` = top + bottom. Used by the `sides` prop of the layout primitives.

aria-activedescendant.description: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

anyOf.description: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be presented if they are made.

aria-braillelabel.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

aria-brailleroledescription.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized abbreviated description for the role of an element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

anyOf.description: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.
Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.
Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

aria-colindextext.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

anyOf.description: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

aria-controls.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

anyOf.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

aria-describedby.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

aria-description.description: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

aria-details.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

anyOf.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.
Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

aria-errormessage.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

anyOf.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

aria-flowto.description: Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion, allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

anyOf.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.
Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.
Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

aria-keyshortcuts.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

aria-label.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

aria-labelledby.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

anyOf.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.
Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.
Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.
Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.
Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.
Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

aria-owns.description: Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

aria-placeholder.description: Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

anyOf.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.
Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.
Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.
Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.
Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

anyOf.description:
Element to render instead of a `div`. Use it to give a region correct semantics (`ul` for a navigator, `nav`/`aside`/`header` for landmarks) without dropping to a raw element.

List elements (`ul`/`ol`/`li`) render with their browser bullet, margin and indent removed — the primitive stays a pure layout box.

Paint the region with a semantic surface token (e.g. `'surfaceMuted'`, `'surfaceSubtle'`, `'background'`). The typed, sanctioned form of the `style={{ background: token }}` escape hatch — use it to give a layout region a surface without wrapping it in a Card. Colour only: text colour stays on the children (`Label color`), and borders/radius belong to Card.

Whether to apply padding to the bottom side.

⚠️ See  {@link  left }  — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer  {@link  sides } .

Custom padding sizes for each side using CSS-like syntax
- 1 value: all sides
- 2 values: [vertical, horizontal] = [top/bottom, left/right]
- 3 values: [top, horizontal, bottom] = [top, left/right, bottom]
- 4 values: [top, right, bottom, left]

When customSize is provided, size and directional props (left/right/top/bottom) are ignored
Absolutely fill the nearest `positioned` ancestor (`position: absolute; inset: 0`) — a full-bleed layer such as a background behind content. Pair with `layer` to control stacking order.
Whether the space should take full height
Anchor the element to the full dynamic viewport height (`100dvh`, with a `100vh` fallback). Use on the outermost shell container.
Whether the space should take full width
Grow to fill the free space of a flex parent (`flex: 1 1 0%`).

Make this region the hover scope for its `reveal="hover"` descendants: they appear while it is hovered or holds keyboard focus. Emits `data-hover-scope` on the element — a row, a card, a message bubble whose actions should show on approach rather than compete with the content.
Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

is.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

anyOf.description: Stacking order for layered children: `back` (behind), `base` (content), `dock` (above). No default — z-index is applied only when set.

Whether to apply padding to the left side.

⚠️ Specifying **any** of `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom` turns every
*unspecified* side **off**. `{ top: false }` therefore means "no padding at all", not "all sides but top". Prefer  {@link  sides } .
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic height by setting `min-height: 0`. Required for a nested scroll area inside a flex column.
Allow shrinking below the content's intrinsic width by setting `min-width: 0`. Required to let a flex child truncate its own children (e.g. an ellipsised Label inside a row).
Click event handler

Make the region transparent to the pointer (`pointer-events: none`), so it frames and positions its children without becoming a hit target itself.

For a full-bleed wrapper whose only job is geometry — a centring band over a canvas, an absolutely-positioned overlay column. Children opt back in with `pointerThrough={false}` on the box that should actually receive events.
Establish a positioning context (`position: relative`) so a `fill` child can absolutely fill it. Use on the layered shell container.

`hover` hides this region (`opacity: 0; pointer-events: none`) until the nearest `hoverScope` ancestor is hovered or focused, or the region itself takes focus — so a keyboard user always reaches it. Where any pointer is coarse (`(any-pointer: coarse)`) it is always shown: touch cannot hover, and a hidden action there would be an invisible tap target. Opacity only — the content stays mounted and in the tab order. `always` is the default.

Whether to apply padding to the right side.

⚠️ See  {@link  left }  — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer  {@link  sides } .
Make the element scroll its overflow (`overflow: auto`) and shrink as a flex child (`min-width/height: 0`), so a scroll region "just works" without the usual min-size incantation.
Scrollbar appearance. Only meaningful together with `scroll`.

Elevation for a layout region, from the `boxShadow` token scale — the typed form of `style={{ boxShadow: token }}`.

Card owns elevation for a *surface* (it also brings a border and a radius). This is for a region that is only a band or a plane: a docked chrome bar separated from the content it floats over, where a Card's border and radius would be wrong. Shadow only — background stays with  {@link  background } .

Whether this element may shrink below its content size as a flex child. `false` pins it (`flex-shrink: 0`) so a neighbouring `grow` region absorbs the deficit instead. Defaults to `true` (the flexbox default).

The sides to pad, listed explicitly. `'x'` = left + right, `'y'` = top + bottom. Wins over `left`/`right`/`top`/`bottom`, and is the recommended form: it says what it means and has no interaction between props.
Padding size

Stick to the top of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; top: 0`). Use for section headers inside a `scroll` region. The element must carry its own background so scrolled content does not show through.
Stick to the bottom of the nearest scroll container (`position: sticky; bottom: 0`). Mirror of `sticky` for a bottom-anchored dock.

Whether to apply padding to the top side.

⚠️ See  {@link  left }  — setting one side turns the unspecified ones off. Prefer  {@link  sides } .

ScrollStyle.description:
Scrollbar appearance for a scrollable layout primitive. A CLOSED set — apps pick a design-system look, never raw scrollbar CSS.
- `native` — the platform scrollbar (default)
- `thin` — slim, theme-tinted bar (semantic `border` colour)
- `hidden` — scrolling works, the bar is not painted

onClick.description: Fires on every click of this tab, including when it is already active (unlike the parent `Tabs`' `onChange`); `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

props.description:
CDU-serializable props for the `TabItem` primitive.

- `value` / `visibility` flow straight from the component (scalar/enum passthrough).
- `title` stands in for the component's `children` (text label).
- `startIcon` / `endIcon` are icon-registry names; the adapter resolves them to   the component's non-serializable `ComponentIconConfig`.
- `badge` is a serializable descriptor (icon referenced by name); the adapter   resolves it to the component's `Omit<BadgeProps, 'size'>`.

anyOf.description: A badge beside the label — a count (`value`), a `dot`, or an icon by name — styled by `variant` and `type`.

endIcon.description: Icon after the label, by its `@simulator-ui-kit/icons` export name; an unknown name shows no icon.

startIcon.description: Icon before the label, by its `@simulator-ui-kit/icons` export name; an unknown name shows no icon.

anyOf.description: Visibility state

onScroll.description: Fires as the table body scrolls; `$event` is the DOM scroll event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onSort.description: Fires when the user clicks the header of a `sortable` column, cycling ascending → descending → unsorted; `$event` is the column's `dataIndex`, falling back to its `key` — the direction is not passed.

React_Key.description: A value which uniquely identifies a node among items in an array.

TableColumnCdu.description: A table column descriptor — the serializable subset of `TableColumn` with header icons by name. `render`/`renderHeader` render-callbacks are not authorable; `title`/`dataIndex` narrow to strings and cells fall back to the `dataIndex` lookup.

anyOf.description: Text alignment for the column

dataIndex.description: Data property name — narrowed to a string (component allows `keyof T`).

endIcon.description: Icon-registry name for the header end icon → `ComponentIconConfig` (adapter resolves).

anyOf.description: Fixed column position
Whether column is hidden
Whether the column is sortable

startIcon.description: Icon-registry name for the header start icon → `ComponentIconConfig` (adapter resolves).

title.description: Header title — narrowed to a string (component allows `ReactNode`).

columnWidth.description: Checkbox utility-column width. Use `'1%'` to preserve flexible space for data columns.

anyOf.description: Whether clicking a non-interactive part of a row toggles selection.

anyOf.description: Whether to show table border
Column descriptors with name-based header icons.
Opaque row array.
Whether to show row hover effect
Loading state

anyOf.description: Row-selection config (callbacks omitted).

Size of the table

onChange.description: Fires when the user clicks a tab other than the current one (re-clicking the active tab does not fire); `$event` is the clicked tab's `value` as a bare string, not `{ value }`.

props.description: CDU props for `Tabs` — the tab bar. The individual tabs are `TabItem` children (see `TabItem.primitive`) coming from the tree; `value` is the active tab.

anyOf.description: Gradient color of active tab
Visual variant of the tabs

onBlur.description: Fires when the field loses focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onChange.description: Fires on every edit of the field's text; `$event` is `{ value }`, the new text as a string — also for the numeric types, after the input is sanitised.

onClear.description: Fires when the clear button (`allowClear`, shown on hover or focus while the field has a value) is clicked; `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful. The field does not empty itself — the chain must reset `value`.

onExpandClick.description: Fires when the expand chevron shown by `expandIcon` is clicked; `$event` is the DOM click event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onFocus.description: Fires when the field receives focus; `$event` is the DOM focus event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onInput.description: Fires on every edit, like `onChange`, but `$event` is the raw DOM input event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful — use `onChange` for the value.

onKeyDown.description: Fires on each key press in the field; `$event` is the DOM keyboard event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.

onKeyUp.description: Fires on each key release in the field; `$event` is the DOM keyboard event, from which an expression cannot read anything useful.
